videoIdeas.title: 5 questions that make you unforgettable in a conversation
videoIdeas.hook: Stop asking people 'so what do you do' — it's why nobody remembers you.
videoIdeas.rationale: Birdtart's networking-questions listicle hit 784k views — the single biggest post across all your competitors. A practical, screenshot-able question list is the format winning hardest right now, and you have zero of it. This drags your public speaking pillar out of the 500-view zone.

videoIdeas.title: How to stop sounding nervous when you speak
videoIdeas.hook: Nervous speakers all make the same three mistakes — and they're fixable in a week.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your actionable how-to content is basically absent — everything is commentary. Doctordaanish's 'how to study effectively' breakdown pulled 108k because it solved one concrete problem. A tight, tactical fix-your-delivery video fills your biggest content gap and is evergreen (saveable/shareable).

videoIdeas.title: The Prophetic definition of a leader nobody teaches you
videoIdeas.hook: Everyone wants influence. The Prophetic model says integrity comes first — here's why that order matters.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your Al-Qawi wal-Ameen post (508 views, 58 likes) had a strong like-to-view ratio, meaning the people who saw it valued it — it just didn't travel. Rebuild it as a punchier standalone hook instead of a caption dump, and lean into it as a series. Leadership is your named pillar but your weakest by volume.

videoIdeas.title: The older I get, the less I argue online
videoIdeas.hook: The older I get, the more I realise winning an argument online costs you more than losing one.
videoIdeas.rationale: Birdtart's two 'the older I get' relatable-mindset videos hit 238k and 55k. That reflective, first-person format is dominating mindset right now. You can own it authentically by tying it to your own pull toward refutation posts (you literally admitted this in your June 1 caption) — self-aware, not preachy.

videoIdeas.title: Your anger about the Ummah is useless without this
videoIdeas.hook: Being loud about injustice isn't leadership. Doing something quietly is.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your political/Ummah commentary is clearly your engagement engine (6134 views on the protest post). But it's all reaction. Convert that same energy into a leadership lesson — channel outrage into action — and you keep the reach of your hot-takes while actually serving your stated niche instead of just refuting people.

videoIdeas.title: I studied how great speakers open — they all do this one thing
videoIdeas.hook: The first 10 seconds of a speech decide if anyone listens. Most people waste them saying thank you.
videoIdeas.rationale: Breakdown/analysis videos (doctordaanish's study system, saffanabanana's writing breakdowns at 400k+) consistently outperform. A speech-opening breakdown plays directly to your public speaking pillar, is inherently visual (you can react to clips), and gives you a repeatable series format.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: This is your all-time top post (6134 views, 211 likes) and it's not a coincidence — the hook takes a clear, confrontational stance ('Can't believe we're still discussing...') that forces a reaction. Taking a side in the first line is what pulls your reach.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 15 comments on 6134 views is a low conversation rate for a post this divisive. You stated the take but didn't hand people a question to argue about. End with a direct prompt ('Tell me why I'm wrong') to convert viewers into commenters, which pushes reach further.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 138 likes on 2106 views is one of your best like-to-view ratios (6.5%) — the 'UAE Hijrah bros' angle is specific and named, and specificity is what made people feel seen enough to like. You're sharpest when you name the exact thing you're critiquing.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 5 comments — the take is so complete it leaves nothing to add. And the caption cuts off mid-sentence ('brag ab'). Front-load the sharpest line into the first sentence and leave the counterargument open so people jump in to defend or pile on.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 58 likes on 508 views (11% ratio) — your highest engagement quality on the list. This is proof your actual leadership pillar content resonates deeply with the people who find it. 'Chase influence before character' is a genuinely strong, tweetable line.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: Only 508 views means it didn't get out of the gate. The hook is buried — 'We often chase influence before character' should be the first 3 seconds on screen, not line one of a caption. And the caption trails into a book reference ('11 Prophetic Qualities...') that reads like a slide, not a hook.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: The topic (leisure vs work, trivialising serious matters) is genuinely in your leadership/mindset lane and shows range beyond pure political reaction.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 883 views and 0 comments — the worst outcome on the list. The caption opens with 'There is a clear difference between...' which is abstract and slow; nobody knows what you're talking about in the first 3 seconds. Worse, you reference a previous video ('I've already spoken about this') which tells new viewers they're missing context and to scroll. Make every post self-contained and lead with the concrete example, not the thesis.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 24 comments on 827 views is your strongest comment-to-view ratio here — the sectarianism angle clearly touched a nerve and drove real discussion, which the algorithm rewards. Emotionally charged, debate-worthy topics are your comment engine.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 42 likes against 24 comments suggests the comments may be more argument than agreement, and the reach still capped at 827. Pair the divisive topic with a constructive resolution in the caption so the debate stays productive and shareable, not just a fight — that's the difference between a controversial post and a viral one.
